speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. To better understand what might be causing these symptoms, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or bowel habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail; those are concerning systemic symptoms. Have you noticed any fever, or have you had any lumps or masses elsewhere on your body besides the lymph nodes? Also, have you experienced any night sweats that soaked your bedding?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of persistent "B" symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), abdominal pain, and painless, fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is highly suspicious for this malignancy. I recommend an immediate CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis followed by a lymph node biopsy. REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis.
